quickSummary: Clemmensen (Zn-Hg/HCl) deoxygenates in acidic conditions (avoid for acid-sensitive groups); Wolff-Kishner (NH₂NH₂/KOH) operates in basic conditions. Tollens' oxidizes both aliphatic and aromatic aldehydes to silver mirrors (2 Ag⁰ ↓). Fehling's oxidizes ALIPHATIC aldehydes only (benzaldehyde is negative). Popoff's rule keeps >C=O with the smaller alkyl group during harsh ketone oxidation.
summary: Master carbonyl deoxygenation pathways, Tollens' and Fehling's diagnostic boundaries, and Popoff's ketone cleavage rule.

conceptBreakdown.title: 5.1 Deoxygenation Reductions: Clemmensen vs Wolff-Kishner

summaryBox.title: Acidic vs Basic Deoxygenation
summaryBox.takeaway: Clemmensen (Zn-Hg/HCl) = Acidic (avoids base-sensitive groups). Wolff-Kishner (NH₂NH₂/KOH) = Basic (avoids acid-sensitive groups like -OH, ethers, alkenes).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
DEOXYGENATION REDUCTION MODES
                                     │
         ┌───────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────┐
         ▼                                                       ▼
  CLEMMENSEN REDUCTION                                    WOLFF-KISHNER REDUCTION
  ├── Reagent: **$\text{Zn-Hg} / \text{Conc. HCl}$**             ├── Reagent: **$\text{NH}_2\text{NH}_2 / \text{KOH in Ethylene Glycol, } \Delta$**
  ├── Environment: **ACIDIC**                             ├── Environment: **BASIC**
  └── Avoid for acid-sensitive groups (*alkenes, esters*) └── Avoid for base-sensitive groups (*halides, esters*)
conceptBreakdown.content: Both methods deoxygenate carbonyl groups ($>\text{C=O}$) into methylene groups ($>\text{CH}_2$). Choice depends entirely on whether the molecule contains acid-sensitive or base-sensitive functional groups.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 5.2 Oxidation Profiles & Popoff's Rule
conceptBreakdown.title: 5.2 Oxidation Profiles & Popoff's Rule
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
ALDEHYDE OXIDATION DIAGNOSTICS
                                     │
         ┌───────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────┐
         ▼                                                       ▼
  TOLLENS' TEST (Silver Mirror)                           FEHLING'S TEST (Red Precipitate)
  Reagent: Ammoniacal $\text{AgNO}_3$ ($[\text{Ag(NH}_3)_2]^+$)    Reagent: Fehling A ($\text{CuSO}_4$) + Fehling B (Rochelle Salt)
  ├── Oxidizes BOTH Aliphatic & Aromatic Aldehydes        ├── Oxidizes **ALIPHATIC Aldehydes ONLY**
  └── Yields **$\text{2 Ag}^0 \downarrow$ (Silver Mirror)**   └── Yields **$\text{Cu}_2\text{O} \downarrow$ (Brick-Red Precipitate)**
                                                              └── *(Benzaldehyde gives NEGATIVE Fehling's test!)*

POPOFF'S RULE:
During oxidative cleavage of unsymmetrical ketones (HNO₃/Δ), the >C=O group remains preferentially with the smaller alkyl group:
CH₃-CO-CH₂CH₂CH₃ ──► CH₃COOH + CH₃CH₂COOH
conceptBreakdown.content:
- **Tollens' Reagent**: Oxidizes both aliphatic and aromatic aldehydes to silver mirror ($2\text{Ag}^0\downarrow$).
- **Fehling's Reagent**: Oxidizes aliphatic aldehydes to brick-red $\text{Cu}_2\text{O}\downarrow$; aromatic aldehydes (e.g. Benzaldehyde) give a NEGATIVE test.
- **Popoff's Rule**: In harsh oxidative cleavage of unsymmetrical ketones, the keto group remains with the smaller alkyl fragment.

quickRevision: Clemmensen reduction uses Zn-Hg / conc. HCl (acidic medium).
Wolff-Kishner uses NH₂NH₂ / KOH in ethylene glycol (basic medium).
Tollens' test oxidizes aliphatic AND aromatic aldehydes (Ag mirror).
Fehling's test oxidizes ALIPHATIC aldehydes ONLY (Cu₂O red ppt; PhCHO fails).
Popoff's rule: >C=O stays with the smaller alkyl group during oxidation.
